messages:
lina: Heads-up — found 3 staging accounts with `admin` role after entitlement sync. Deploys got blocked when we toggled the canary. Anyone else seeing this? cc @jen @olivia

sam: I hit the same during the 09:15 canary. Endpoints returned 403s from the deployer. Quick `gcloud` check shows `group:staging-admins` had two service principals that shouldn't be there.

miguel: Did the entitlement job get rerun last night? I triggered a manual sync intended for prod-only yesterday evening.

accessbot: entitlement-sync: completed 2026-03-20T23:10:12Z — changes: +3 bindings in projects/staging (service-account:ci-runner@...), -0.

jen: Paging secops — can we get audit logs + KMS access correlation for the window around the sync? Need to confirm no keys were used or leaked. @secops-bot

secops-bot: Querying audit logs for resource=projects/staging, range=2026-03-20T22:00Z..2026-03-21T00:00Z. ETA ~45s.

olivia: If it's an entitlement-side bug, we should blacklist service accounts that are prod-only from ever being mapped into staging. Also check the mapping source — suspicious that a `prod` include crossed into `staging`.

devops-bot: deploy-canary: automatically reverted at 2026-03-21T09:20Z due to permission errors. Incident ref: INC-6421.

miguel: Found the root cause: the sync lambda pulled a stale mapping file from S3. `mappings/staging.yml` contained an accidental include `- prod-extras` (merge mistake). I removed the include and will push a corrected file.

lina: Ok. Can we run a quick sanity script before re-enabling canary? Something like `scripts/verify-entitlements.sh staging` to ensure no cross-env bindings.

sam: I can run that now and smoke the deploy if it looks clean. Will paste output.

jen: Action items: 1) miguel — fix mapping and tighten S3 ACLs; 2) sam — run verify script + smoke deploy; 3) olivia — add a unit test in entitlement pipeline to detect cross-env includes; 4) jen/secops — run KMS access correlation and confirm no key use.

lina: Also propose a repo-level CI gate that blocks PRs which reference manifests from other env directories (simple lint rule). Make it required for entitlement pipeline.

secops-bot: Audit logs complete. Summary: no KMS Decrypt/Encrypt calls by the affected service accounts in the queried window. No anomalous token creation.

miguel: Pushed fix to S3: `s3://infra-config/mappings/staging.yml` cleaned (removed `prod-extras`). Ran `entitlement-tool validate --env=staging` => OK. Ran dry-run sync => no unexpected bindings.

sam: Ran `verify-entitlements.sh staging` (attached output snippet) and then a smoke canary (2 instances). Both instances deployed successfully, no 403s.

lina: :thumbsup: I'll re-enable the rolling canary to continue the rollout.

olivia: I'll add the unit test + a lint rule to the entitlement repo and open a PR with coverage.

jen: I'll file a short post-incident note and a small follow-up ticket to add weekly random spot-checks of mapping files. Recommend we add a guardrail around S3 object immutability for mapping files (versioned writes only).

lina: Thanks everyone. Quick runbook note for future: 1) if canary hits 403s, check `entitlement-sync` events, then `s3://infra-config/mappings/<env>.yml` for accidental includes, then run `entitlement-tool validate --env=<env>`. Add the runbook to oncall playbook.

jen: Closing loop — assigning entitlement pipeline hardening to next sprint and marking INC-6421 resolved pending PR reviews. Thanks all.
